own_original_text:
Whereas, the Federal Alcohol Control Administration has submitted for my approval, an Amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry, and has rendered its report and recommendations and findings thereon:

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby find:

1. That an application has been duly made, pursuant to and in full compliance with the provisions of the Act and of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry, for my approval of an Amendment to the said Code; and

2. That due notice and opportunity for hearing to interested parties have been given pursuant to the provisions of the Act and regulations thereunder; and

3. That hearings have been held upon the Amendment pursuant to such notice and the provisions of the Act and regulations thereunder; and

4. That said Code of Fair Competition as hereby amended will constitute a Code of Fair Competition as contemplated by the Act and complies in all respects with pertinent provisions of the Act, including Section 3(a) of Title I thereof; and

5. That it appears, after due consideration, that said Code as hereby amended will tend to effectuate the policy of Congress as declared in Section 1 of Title I of the Act; and

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, pursuant to the authority vested in me by Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby approve said Amendment and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry by Executive Order dated November 26, 1933, and my previous approval of the said Code as amended by Executive Order dated June 29, 1934, to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

August 4, 1934.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 6811 (August 4, 1934) is a approval of an amendment to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry and modification of the earlier approvals to cover the code as amended under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (page record checked; identity, date and subject confirmed against the census register and the WPA 1944 list); the order's own text states no limit on the approval. Its command depends entirely on the code approval, so its first end is the repeal of the code-approval and code-enforcement provisions of Title I by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no period, \"until\" date, condition or provisional approval that limits the approval, and no stay or postponement to a fixed date. Held later orders naming the code are EO 7000 (April 5, 1935) and EO 7018 (April 19, 1935); the earlier approvals are EO 6444 (November 26, 1933) and EO 6756-D (June 29, 1934). I read the operative sentence of each: each approves amendments and modifies the previous approval to include an approval of the code in its entirety as amended. None cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes the approval, so each later order is a later event. No held text cites this order by number. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command. June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.","independent_command_check":"No appointment, delegation, direction to a government agency, report direction or other command independent of the code approval appears. The \"Approval recommended\" and signature lines command nothing.","savings_check":"Read S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso and NIRA section 5 in the packet excerpts. No held source continues this approval, a prosecution under it or any command of this order after June 14, 1935; accrued acts, liabilities and the section 5 exemption for completed action are recorded as transferred or accrued and not as continued operation.","scope_check":"The machine inventory has five clauses, items 1 to 5, which are the President's numbered findings (application made, notice, hearings held, the code as amended complies with section 3(a), the policy of Congress) and, at the end of item 5, the final approval. Findings command nothing. The only operative command is the final sentence approving the amendment and modifying the earlier approvals, which is the single corrected clause (inventory correction recorded). The held text does not reproduce the amendment; its content is not needed because it takes effect only as a term of the code approved under section 3."}

savings_residuals.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.
